AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JANUARY 18, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDER N-15-21, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE
FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING: YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO:
publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING
THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709
573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER
CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION  PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9(d)(4) in one case.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - EXISTING LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT
  CODE §54956.9(d)(1) City of Norwalk vs. Regional Water Quality Control Board, Case No.
  21STCP04148.

  III.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  IV.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk City Employees Association.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Danny Casas Jr.
  Senior Executive Pastor Remnant Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Leo Martinez
  Student

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize the Angel Tree and Stuff A Bus donors.

  II.  City Council to recognize the families who painted Christmas designs on City Hall windows.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.
   2.  Dr. Jose Fierro to make a presentation on Cerritos College.

  3.  Las Posadas event video.

  4.  Recognition of a Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department Homicide Detective and two Sergeants.

  5.  Public Safety and Traffic Concerns.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of
  December 21, 2021. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the periods November 28, 2021 –
  December 11, 2021, in the total amount of $946,346.46; and December 12, 2021 – December 25,
  2021, in the total amount of $918,066.99. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  December 16, 2021 – January 12, 2022, in the total amount of $5,011,953.10. 640

  Report

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Melanie Caraan
  and Lisa Hawkins. 830-03/08

  Report

  5.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-01 – DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – CITY CLERK
  DEPARTMENT - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-01, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN
  RECORDS IN THE CITY CLERK DEPARTMENT. 870-02

  Report

  6.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-03 - FACSIMILE SIGNATURES - Staff recommends City Council adopt
  Resolution No. 22-03, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AUTHORIZING AND DIRECTING CERTAIN BANKS TO HONOR ALL CHECKS, DRAFTS, AND
  WARRANTS WHEN BEARING CERTAIN SIGNATURES AND FACSIMILE SIGNATURES OF CITY
  OFFICIALS AS DESIGNATED AND RESCINDING ALL CONFLICTING RESOLUTIONS. 602

  Report

  7.  RESOLUTION NOS. 22-04 AND 22-05 – APPOINTMENT OF MEMBERS OF THE CITY COUNCIL TO
  THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY CITY SELECTION COMMITTEE/EASTERN REGION AND THE LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY SANITATION DISTRICT NOS. 2 AND 18 – Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 22-04, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  DESIGNATING MAYOR RICK RAMIREZ AS THE CITY’S REPRESENTATIVE AND VICE MAYOR
  ANA VALENCIA AS THE ALTERNATE FOR THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY CITY SELECTION
  COMMITTEE/EASTERN REGION; and

  b.  Resolution No. 22-05, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPOINTING COUNCILMEMBER JENNIFER PEREZ AS THE CITY’S ALTERNATE TO THE
  LOS ANGELES COUNTY SANITATION DSTRICT NOS. 2 AND 18. 825-09

  Report
   8.  CONFIRM PRECISION PIPELINE INC. EMERGENCY WORK AT SEVERAL LOCATIONS WITHIN
  THE CITY OF NORWALK AND THE CITY OF ARTESIA - Staff recommends City Council confirm the
  emergency service repair work for the locations listed in the attached summary, completed by Precision
  Pipeline, Inc., in the amount of $18,158.84. 955

  Report

  9.  ACCEPTANCE OF WORK FOR BATTERY ELECTRIC BUS CHARGING INFRASTRUCTURE AND
  INSTALLATION OF FOUR BATTERY ELECTRIC BUS CHARGERS - Staff recommends City Council
  accept the work of Elecnor Belco Electric, Inc. in the amount of $102,155.91 for the Construction of
  Battery Electric Bus Infrastructure and installation of four Electric Bus Chargers. 634-03

  Report

  10. APPOINTMENT OF MEMBERS OF THE CITY COUNCIL TO VARIOUS AGENCIES AND ADVISORY
  BODIES – Staff recommends City Council confirm the nominations as presented. 825-09

  Report

  11. ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  12. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200 RESOLUTIONS

  Report

  13. PROJECT NO. 7930 – AWARD CONTRACTS FOR CONSTRUCTION AND CONSTRUCTION
  SUPPORT SERVICES FOR COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT FUNDED LOCAL
  STREET REHABILITATIONS AND RESOLUTION NO. 22-02 - BUDGET AMENDMENT - ENGINEER’S
  REPORT NO. 21-22 – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-02, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE ROAD MAINTENANCE REHABILITATION ACCOUNT, AND
  TRANSPORTATION DEVELOPMENT ACT ARTICLE 3 FUNDS FOR PROJECT NO. 7930 -
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT FUNDED LOCAL STREET REHABILITATION, in
  the amounts of $41,758 and $174,000, respectively;

  b.  award a contract to All American Asphalt for the Community Development Block Grant funded
  Local Street Rehabilitation in the amount of $1,041,470; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the contract and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget and it is within
  the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney;
  and

  c.  approve an agreement with Z&K Consultants, Inc. of San Bernardino, in an amount not to exceed
  $99,312 for construction management and inspection services for the Community Development
  Block Grant funded Local Street Rehabilitation; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget and it is within the City
  Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.
  610/1005-04-7930

  Report
   14. RESOLUTION NO. 22-06 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – ADD LOW AND MODERATE INCOME
  HOUSING ASSET FUNDS FOR CONTRACT SERVICES AND APPROVE ADDITIONAL SERVICES
  FOR PROJECT MANAGEMENT, URBAN DESIGN, SPECIFIC PLAN AND PUBLIC OUTREACH FOR
  PROJECT NO. 7859 – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-06, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO ADD LOW AND MODERATE INCOME HOUSING ASSET FUNDS FOR PROJECT
  MANAGEMENT, URBAN DESIGN, SPECIFIC PLAN AND PUBLIC OUTREACH SERVICES FOR
  THE CALIFORNIA YOUTH AUTHORITY PROPERTY FOR CITY PROJECT NO. 7859, in the
  amount of $840,000; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute an amendment to the agreement with CSG Consultants,
  Inc. for additional identified services and such other services reasonably necessary thereto as
  determined by the City Manager related to the California Youth Authority property, City Project No.
  7859, not-to-exceed $840,000, provided there is funding in the budget, separate from the existing
  contract compensation, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 610/1005-04-7859

  Report

  15. RESOLUTION NO. 22-08 – BUDGET AMENDMENT AND AWARD CONTRACT FOR CONSULTING
  SERVICES FOR PREPARATION OF A SEWER SYSTEM MANAGEMENT PLAN - Staff recommends
  City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-08, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE AVAILABLE ENTERPRISE FUNDS FOR THE PREPARATION OF A
  SEWER SYSTEM MANAGEMENT PLAN, in the amount of $68,550; and

  b.  award a contract to AKM Consulting Engineers, in the amount of $160,524 to provide professional
  consulting services for the preparation of a Sewer System Management Plan; and authorize the
  City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding in the
  budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 610/1040-07

  Report

REPORTS

  16. EMPLOYEE INCENTIVE CAMPAIGN FOR ATTRACTING AND RETAINING NORWALK TRANSIT
  SYSTEM FULL-TIME/PART-TIME TRANSIT BUS OPERATORS - Staff recommends City Council
  approve the Department of Transportation a Transit employee referral program for $500 for Part-time
  Bus Operator candidates who complete six months of employment. 1120-13

  Report

  17. 2021-2029 DRAFT HOUSING ELEMENT UPDATE – Staff recommends City Council provide input
  and/or express concerns to staff regarding the Draft Housing Element to address the California
  Department of Housing and Community Development comments and to receive and file this report.
  320-02-03

  Report

  18. RESOLUTION NO. 22-07 – CITY OF NORWALK HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN – Staff recommends
  City Council approve adopt Resolution No. 22-07, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF NORWALK ADOPTING THE NORWALK HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN. 710-03

  Report

  19. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – JANUARY EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE - Receive
  and file. 710-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
 ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated January 14, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
